title: Knife Mastery & Prep Work
description: Master essential knife cuts, grip techniques, and kitchen safety basics.

skills.name: Knife Safety & Control
skills.shortDescription: Learn safe knife handling, a stable grip, and basic cuts to prepare ingredients efficiently and reduce the risk of accidents.

coreSteps.title: Claw Grip
coreSteps.description: Curl your fingertips inward and use your knuckles to guide the side of the blade while holding food steady.

coreSteps.title: Pinch Grip
coreSteps.description: Pinch the blade near the handle with your thumb and index finger, then wrap your remaining fingers around the handle for control.

coreSteps.title: Controlled Cuts
coreSteps.description: Use slow, deliberate cuts and keep the cutting board stable. Choose a chopping motion or a gentle rocking motion that suits the ingredient and knife.

keyTypesOrCuts: Rough Chop: Larger, irregular pieces for dishes where uniformity is less important.
Dice: Small, similarly sized cubes that cook at a more even rate.
Mince: Very small pieces, commonly used for garlic, ginger, and herbs.
Slice: Thin, even pieces of vegetables, fruit, or other ingredients.
safetyOrProTips: Place a damp towel beneath the cutting board to help prevent it from sliding.
Keep fingertips curled away from the blade and cut slowly until your technique feels comfortable.
A sharp, well-maintained knife is generally safer than a dull knife because it requires less force.
skills.whereItsUsed: Most recipes that require preparing vegetables, fruit, herbs, or other ingredients.

title: Heat & Pan Control
description: Learn to manage stovetop heat and use a pan to sauté, sear, and cook ingredients evenly without burning them.

skills.name: Stovetop Heat & Pan Techniques
skills.shortDescription: Learn how to preheat a pan, choose an appropriate heat level, and control cooking so ingredients brown evenly instead of burning or steaming.

coreSteps.title: Preheat the Pan
coreSteps.description: Warm the pan over an appropriate heat before adding ingredients. Add oil when suitable for the recipe, and avoid letting an empty pan overheat.

coreSteps.title: Choose the Right Heat
coreSteps.description: Use low heat for gentle cooking, medium heat for many everyday sautéing tasks, and higher heat when a recipe calls for a quick sear. Adjust as the food cooks.

coreSteps.title: Avoid Crowding the Pan
coreSteps.description: Leave space between ingredients so moisture can escape and the food can brown. Cook in batches if necessary.

coreSteps.title: Sauté and Sear
coreSteps.description: Sauté smaller pieces with a little oil, moving or tossing them as needed. For searing, let the food make contact with the hot pan long enough to develop browning before turning.

keyTypesOrCuts: Sautéing: Cooking ingredients relatively quickly with a small amount of fat.
Searing: Browning the surface of food using sufficiently high heat.
Pan-Frying: Cooking food in a shallow layer of oil, turning as needed.
safetyOrProTips: Keep pan handles turned inward so they are less likely to be bumped.
Food added to a pan can cause oil to splatter, especially when wet; pat ingredients dry when appropriate.
Lower the heat if oil smokes or ingredients brown too quickly.
skills.whereItsUsed: Stir-fries, eggs, sautéed vegetables, skillet meals, and many stovetop proteins.

title: Boiling & Simmering
description: Learn to control bubbling liquid to cook pasta, grains, eggs, and soups with the right texture.

skills.name: Boiling & Simmering Control
skills.shortDescription: Recognize the difference between a rolling boil and a gentle simmer, and choose the right liquid temperature for the food you're cooking.

coreSteps.title: Bring Liquid to a Boil
coreSteps.description: Heat water or another cooking liquid until bubbles rise actively across the surface. Use a lid to help it heat faster, keeping an eye on the pot.

coreSteps.title: Adjust to a Simmer
coreSteps.description: Reduce the heat until small, gentle bubbles appear occasionally or steadily, depending on the recipe.

coreSteps.title: Add Food at the Right Time
coreSteps.description: Follow the recipe's instructions about when to add pasta, eggs, grains, or other ingredients; different foods start in hot or cold liquid.

coreSteps.title: Check Texture and Timing
coreSteps.description: Stir when needed and begin checking the food near the recipe's suggested cooking time. Drain or remove it once it reaches the desired texture.

keyTypesOrCuts: Rolling Boil: Vigorous bubbling, often used for pasta and blanching vegetables.
Gentle Simmer: Small, controlled bubbles, often used for soups, stews, and gentle poaching.
Blanching: Briefly boiling food, often followed by cooling it quickly to help preserve texture and color.
safetyOrProTips: Use a pot large enough to reduce the chance of liquid boiling over.
Lower the heat once a steady boil is reached if the recipe does not require vigorous boiling.
Lift pot lids carefully and angle them away from your face to avoid steam burns.
skills.whereItsUsed: Pasta, rice and other grains, boiled eggs, soups, stews, and blanched vegetables.

title: Mixing & Whisking
description: Build confidence combining ingredients smoothly and evenly with spoons, forks, whisks, and bowls.

skills.name: Mixing, Whisking & Combining
skills.shortDescription: Learn how to combine ingredients evenly, break up lumps, and whisk mixtures to the consistency a recipe needs.

coreSteps.title: Choose the Right Tool
coreSteps.description: Use a fork or whisk for eggs and thin mixtures, a spoon or spatula for folding and stirring, and a larger bowl when ingredients need room to move.

coreSteps.title: Whisk Until Combined
coreSteps.description: Move the whisk through the mixture in quick circular or back-and-forth strokes, scraping the sides of the bowl when needed to incorporate everything evenly.

coreSteps.title: Mix Without Overdoing It
coreSteps.description: Mix until ingredients are combined unless the recipe calls for a specific texture. For batters, overmixing can make some baked goods tough.

coreSteps.title: Fold Delicate Ingredients
coreSteps.description: Use a spatula to gently lift and turn ingredients when you want to combine them without deflating a light mixture or breaking delicate pieces.

keyTypesOrCuts: Stirring: Moving ingredients together with a spoon or spatula.
Whisking: Beating a mixture to combine ingredients and, when appropriate, incorporate air.
Folding: Gently turning ingredients together to preserve a light or delicate texture.
Mashing: Pressing soft foods, such as cooked potatoes or bananas, into a smoother mixture.
safetyOrProTips: Use a bowl with enough space to prevent splashes and spills.
Crack eggs into a separate small bowl first when you want to check for shell fragments before adding them to a larger mixture.
Scrape the bowl's sides and bottom so dry or unmixed ingredients are not left behind.
skills.whereItsUsed: Scrambled eggs, oatmeal, batters, dressings, marinades, dips, and many baking recipes.

title: Oven Roasting & Baking
description: Learn the basics of oven cooking, from preparing a tray to roasting ingredients evenly.

skills.name: Oven Roasting & Baking Basics
skills.shortDescription: Learn how to prepare ingredients for the oven, use the correct temperature and rack position, and recognize when food is ready.

coreSteps.title: Preheat the Oven
coreSteps.description: Set the oven to the recipe's stated temperature and allow it to preheat before putting the food in, unless the recipe says otherwise.

coreSteps.title: Prepare the Tray or Dish
coreSteps.description: Use the pan or baking dish specified by the recipe. Line or lightly oil it when appropriate, and arrange ingredients so heat can circulate.

coreSteps.title: Arrange Food Evenly
coreSteps.description: Cut ingredients into similar sizes and spread them in a single layer when roasting. Crowding a tray can trap moisture and reduce browning.

coreSteps.title: Check Progress Safely
coreSteps.description: Use the recipe's timing as a guide, check food as it cooks, and rotate the tray if needed for more even results. Use oven mitts when handling hot cookware.

keyTypesOrCuts: Roasting: Cooking foods, often vegetables or proteins, in the oven to develop browning and flavor.
Baking: Cooking foods such as casseroles, breads, and baked dishes using oven heat.
Sheet-Pan Cooking: Preparing ingredients together on a tray, often for a convenient one-pan meal.
safetyOrProTips: Use dry oven mitts and keep hands and forearms clear of hot oven surfaces.
Avoid overcrowding the tray when browning is important.
For meat, poultry, and fish, follow reliable food-safety guidance rather than relying on color alone to determine doneness.
skills.whereItsUsed: Roasted vegetables and potatoes, baked fish or chicken, casseroles, and sheet-pan meals.
